news.title: New agentic memory framework uses 118K tokens per query. LangMem burns through 3.26M.
news.summary_raw: Long-horizon reasoning exposes a core weakness in AI agents: context windows fill up fast, and retrieval pipelines return noise instead of signal.To solve this, researchers at the National University of Singapore developed MRAgent, a framework that abandons the static "retrieve-then-reason" approach. Instead, it uses a mechanism that allows an agent to dynamically develop its memory based on accumulating evidence. This multi-step memory reconstruction is integrated into the reasoning p
news.summary: Researchers at the National University of Singapore have developed MRAgent, a new agentic memory framework that dynamically develops an agent's memory based on accumulating evidence, using a multi-step memory reconstruction process. This framework can handle large amounts of information, using up to 118K tokens per query, and is more efficient than traditional retrieval pipelines, which return noise instead of signal.

news.title: Talos: Scaling rare disease diagnosis with automated, iterative genomic reanalysis
news.summary_raw:
Talos was built to help resolve a major bottleneck in genomic medicine: human review time. The open-source system recovered 90% of in-scope diagnoses while surfacing just 1.3 candidate variants per patient for expert review. 
The post Talos: Scaling rare disease diagnosis with automated, iterative genomic reanalysis appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed Talos, an open-source system that uses automated genomic reanalysis to recover 90% of in-scope diagnoses, with just 1.3 candidate variants per patient. This could streamline human review time in genomic medicine.
